ca_south_san_diego_county.blurb: This part of San Diego County lies south of Highway 52 and mixes small urban crags with bigger inland mountains and boulder fields. Sport, bouldering and trad are close to evenly split, with a little top rope, aid and alpine on the side. Roped climbing is concentrated around 5.10 and 5.11 with a solid run of easier lines below, while the boulder problems run from V0 up through the mid grades with a few hard ones. El Cajon Mountain has granite sport and multi-pitch trad, though the hike in is in direct sun. Mission Gorge offers trad and top rope, and its west-facing walls are shaded in the morning. Santee Boulders is the beginner-friendly bouldering hub.

co_denver_south.blurb: South of Denver, this region is dominated by Castlewood Canyon, a shallow canyon on the western edge of the plains that Cherry Creek has cut southeast of the city. The cliffs here are short and fairly steep, and the rock changes from crumbly shale to conglomerate and sandstone, so quality varies from wall to wall. Bouldering makes up the bulk of the climbs, with sport, trad and top rope each making a smaller share. Grades are broad: boulder problems from V0 into the double digits, and roped climbs clustered around 5.10 and 5.11 with plenty of easier options. A small waterfall and the north side of the canyon can form ice in cold, damp winters. Rattlesnakes are common in summer.

pa_southeastern_lowlands.blurb: These are the rolling lowlands of southeastern Pennsylvania around Philadelphia, with crags scattered along rivers and creeks and a good deal of urban climbing in the city itself. Bouldering is by far the largest share, with sport next and a smaller amount of trad and top rope; a few ice lines form at The Narrows in winter. Boulder problems cover everything from V0 into the low double digits, while roped climbs mostly sit between 5.7 and 5.11. Haycock Mountain near Lake Nockamixon has woodland bouldering on diabase boulders. Ralph Stover State Park offers trad and top rope above Tohickon Creek, and Birdsboro Quarry is the place for bolted sport lines.

or_portland_the_gorge.blurb: This region covers the Portland metro area and the Columbia Gorge on the Oregon side, so most of its crags are a short drive from the city. Bouldering is the largest share, followed by sport and trad, with some top rope. Roped grades center on 5.10 to 5.12 with a decent supply of moderates, and boulder problems run from easy to hard but are weighted toward V2 to V5. Basalt is the rock at Broughton Bluff and Viento. Broughton Bluff, hidden under tree cover, stays cool and shady in summer and can be climbed year-round when dry. Viento Wall is steep, blocky and overhanging. Rocky Butte, Madrone Wall and Carver are other sizeable crags.

ut_big_cottonwood_canyon.blurb: Big Cottonwood is a long V-shaped canyon in the Wasatch Range, roughly twelve miles southeast of Salt Lake City. Hundreds of routes are spread across dozens of crags on both sides of the road, mostly on quartzite that is hard and slippery, with holds sticking out at odd angles. Trad and sport are about evenly matched, with a smaller number of boulder problems and a handful of ice lines that tend to form late and melt early. Most roped climbs fall between 5.7 and 5.12, with a heavy middle around 5.10. S-Curves is a popular bolted area known for overhanging routes. Other larger spots include Storm Mountain Picnic Area, Challenge Buttress and Brighton.

ut_boulders_little_cottonwood.blurb: Little Cottonwood Canyon is a steep-walled canyon with a river and forest, about twenty minutes from downtown Salt Lake City, and it is a major bouldering destination. The problems are almost all boulders and span the whole range, with a big pool of easy and moderate lines and plenty of hard ones up to the top end. The rock is quartz monzonite, often called granite: lower down it has crystal-heavy slopers and crimps, higher up it is more tightly grained and friction-reliant. Secret Garden at the bottom suits beginners, while White Pine, higher and shaded by trees, is the summer pick. Fall and spring are the prime seasons, and the sunnier north side dries fastest.
